A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HSRDM research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-G are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original forecasting and segmentation experiments on FigureEight, basketball, MarchingBand and soldier recordings.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds a recurrence ablation, SNLDS comparisons and synthetic scaling experiments.

M1.justification: The hierarchical states, recurrent transitions, autoregressive emissions, variational updates, initialization and forecasting procedures remain unchanged. Expanded explanations of covariates and learnable recurrence parameters document existing capabilities.

E1.justification: The four original application domains remain. Appendices F.3-F.4 add simplified MarchingBand scenarios without the reset state C, including noisy higher-dimensional observations. These introduce different input conditions and remove one coordination requirement.

E2.justification: v3 adds independently fitted SNLDS models to the basketball comparison in Table 1 and Figure 3. FigureEight also gains a no-recurrence comparator, previously evaluated on other tasks. Existing comparator memberships are retained.

E3.justification: New SNLDS experiments specify 10 discrete states, continuous latent dimension 4 and 20,000 training iterations with 1,000 warm-up iterations. New scaling protocols use 200 entities or 10/30-dimensional observations and five system states. Original splits, forecasting windows and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D.3 adds an explicit test of recurrence's contribution to FigureEight forecasting. Appendices F.3-F.4 introduce group-size and feature-dimension sensitivity studies, including accuracy and runtime plots. Together these substantially expand component and scalability analyses beyond v2.

E5.justification: Appendix F.4 newly reports mean segmentation accuracy with standard-deviation error bars across five initializations; v2's MarchingBand results reported best and median accuracy. Existing experiments retain their run counts, forecast uncertainty reporting and basketball hypothesis-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Existing main comparison scores are retained, but substantial results are added: FigureEight no-recurrence best/average MSE of 0.05/2.41; SNLDS basketball errors of 17.2/16.0/16.1 feet for 1/5/20 training games; and scaling results. Appendix F.3 reports 100% best/median and 90% mean accuracy at 200 entities; F.4 reports means of 88%/80%/75% for dimensions 2/10/30. The scaling experiments omit C, so these are not same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: The filtering and smoothing propositions, proofs, variational derivations and forecasting mathematics remain substantively unchanged. Section 2 rearranges the joint-density display using the same factors rather than introducing a different mathematical model.

C1.justification: The introduction adds a claimed benefit of recurrence: state-duration distributions more expressive than geometric distributions. The central contributions concerning hierarchical coordination, efficient inference, competitive forecasting and interpretability remain.

C2.justification: Section 6 substantially expands applicability and limitations: discrete representations and indirect interactions can restrict expressivity, while clear top-down coordination and limited data may favor HSRDM. It adds hypotheses explaining GroupNet's basketball advantage and identifies circumstances favoring alternatives. The soldier study is explicitly framed as interpreting one model's fit.

D1.justification: Appendix E.2 adds SNLDS implementation and configuration references, architecture, warm-up and convergence-check details. Appendices F.3-F.4 document scaling settings and noise construction. Existing HSRDM code access and the restriction on sharing soldier data remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4 expands interaction-graph positioning to learned edge types, GRASS and scalable graph inference, adding relevant works such as Liu et al. (2023) and Wang and Pang (2024). Sanchez-Gonzalez et al. (2020) is removed, and SNLDS is explicitly categorized as recurrent. The broader positioning remains.

P1.justification: v3 edits model explanations, experimental prose, terminology and cross-references, and adds a Broader Impacts section. Publication headers and reference formatting change, while the principal section order and appendix organization remain.

P2.justification: Figure 2's table and Table 1/Figure 3 expand for new comparators. Figures D.1 and F.1 are added, Figure 4's ablation labels are clarified, and existing material reflows within the publication layout. Most original graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical support through the FigureEight recurrence control, SNLDS basketball comparison and scaling studies, while Section 6 better explains the model's limitations and appropriate uses. These are useful, bounded improvements: the scaling studies remove the reset state, limiting their validation of the complete coordination task, and the original method and main results remain stable.
